stem.text: Let \( y = f(x) \) be a twice-differentiable function. Suppose that \( f'(3) = 8 \). Write this statement in Leibniz notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( \left. \frac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=3} = 8 \), so the rate of change of y with respect to x when x = 3 is 8.

worked_solution.text: In \( f'(3) \) the function is f, the independent variable is x, and the derivative is evaluated at x = 3, so the statement is about one input only.
In Leibniz notation the same statement is \( \left. \frac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=3} = 8 \).
It says that the rate of change of y with respect to x when x = 3 is 8.

options.label: \( \frac{f(3)}{3} = 8 \), so y divided by x when x = 3 is 8.
options.derivation: the Leibniz fraction read as the quotient of the two quantities at the point

options.label: \( \left. \frac{dx}{dy} \right|_{x=3} = 8 \), so the rate of change of x with respect to y when x = 3 is 8.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable

options.label: \( \left. \frac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=3} = 8 \), so the rate of change of y with respect to x when x = 3 is 8.
\( \frac{dy}{dx} = 8 \), so the rate of change of y with respect to x, the same at every x, is 8.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the derivative function
